data.description:
## Reproduction

1. Orchestrator dispatches a sub-agent with `isolation: "worktree"` (e.g., for parallel impl tasks within a sprint).
2. The Agent runtime creates a worktree under `/Users/joeoakhart/digital-service-orchestra/.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>/`.
3. Sub-agent receives the task prompt and (intended) CWD inside the worktree.
4. Sub-agent invokes file-writing tools (Edit, Write) using full absolute paths that resolve to the ORCHESTRATOR's session worktree (e.g., `/Users/joeoakhart/digital-service-orchestra-worktrees/worktree-20260519-131000/...`) instead of its own isolated worktree path.
5. Sub-agent reports CONFIDENT and its agent worktree is empty/clean at harvest time, while session worktree shows uncommitted changes that the orchestrator then has to commit.

## Expected

Sub-agent file-writing tools should resolve relative paths against the agent worktree's CWD, OR the dispatcher should ensure absolute path usage targets the agent worktree path. Either the agent's runtime or the prompt-resolution layer should fence file writes to the agent's worktree path.

## Actual

Sub-agents frequently 'leak' writes back to the session worktree. Empirically observed during epic f691-681e (PR #245) across at least 7 sub-agent dispatches: S7.T7, S7.T8, S7.T9, S_docs.T1, S_docs.T2, S_docs.T3, SC3-remediation. (S7.T6, S7.T10, S7.T11 isolated cleanly — pattern is NOT deterministic.)

## Evidence

- Session worktree status after dispatching 5 parallel sub-agents (S7.T7-T11) with isolation:"worktree" showed:
  - T7 worktree: empty (git status clean) — but session worktree had M runner.py, conftest.py, test_runner_smoke.py
  - T8 worktree: empty — but session worktree had ?? check-fp-recovery-eligibility.sh + M SKILL.md, FP-RECOVERY-WORKFLOW.md + .test-index
  - T9 worktree: never created (no worktreePath returned in dispatch output) — but session worktree had ?? test_dso_ci_review_large_diff_e2e.py
  - T10 worktree: HAD its changes (CI-INTEGRATION.md + CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md)
  - T11 worktree: HAD its changes (verify-session-provenance.sh + .test-index)
- Memory file feedback_worktree_subagent_pitfalls.md (2026-05-02) documents this pattern as recurring across multiple sprints. No bug ticket existed before now.

## Cost

Per session: ~30 min of inspection time spent figuring out which changes are in which worktree. Per dispatch: orchestrator must run `git status` on both session AND each agent worktree to figure out where changes landed before committing.

## Hypothesis

Suspect that when the sub-agent's task prompt contains absolute paths to the session worktree (e.g., for reading reference files), the agent's subsequent file writes inherit those absolute paths rather than its own worktree's CWD. Or: the runtime's CWD switch to the agent worktree may not happen for all dispatch shapes.

## Proposed investigation

1. Capture the exact sub-agent prompt + initial CWD + worktree path for each dispatch.
2. Add a diagnostic step at sub-agent start: `echo "CWD: $(pwd); REPO_ROOT: $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` so post-run we know what the agent SAW.
3. Audit the dispatch prompt template (worktree-dispatch.md) for explicit absolute-path patterns that could be the trigger.

## Related

- Memory file: feedback_worktree_subagent_pitfalls.md (2026-05-02) — documents this and 4 other worktree pitfalls.
- Bug 9679-695c-6e11-4d95 — sub-agent dispatch in branch-isolated mode lacks branch-context verification. Same root area, different symptom.
data.title: [sub-agent dispatch]: isolation:worktree -> sub-agent writes to session worktree instead of its isolation worktree (leakage pattern)
